scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8841: Users report that "web0.local" and "web1.local" will not
load at all from host_1_1_1_1 -- the portals never come up. The team has decided
that all the web servers in the server farm must have crashed and wants every
web server rebooted. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the web servers, but the web servers are healthy: web_server_0
(10.200.0.3) and the other web servers are UP, reachable at the IP layer (ping
succeeds), and Apache is still serving HTTP on port 80. The symptom is purely
dead name resolution, not a web-server crash and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the web servers: they answer HTTP when
reached by IP, so the user's "all the web servers crashed" hypothesis is wrong.
An agent that reboots / blames web_server_0 (or the other web servers) has
followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The web servers need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the **BIND 9 (`named`) DNS daemon** on `dns_server` (10.200.0.2). The daemon was in a systemd `failed` state — it had not been running at all since the lab started (the service is marked enabled but the unit showed `Active: failed`).

**Mechanism:** Both `host_1_1_1_1` and the rest of the network relied on `dns_server` as their sole nameserver (configured via `/etc/resolv.conf` → `nameserver 10.200.0.2`). With `named` down, every DNS query returned "connection refused" on port 53. Because `web0.local` and `web1.local` are names in the `.local` authoritative zone served by this BIND instance, they could not be resolved — hence the portals would never load. IP-level connectivity was completely intact: `host_1_1_1_1` could successfully ping `web_server_0` (10.200.0.3) and `web_server_1` (10.200.0.4) by address, and all four Apache instances were running and listening on port 80 normally.

**Localization:** Solely `dns_server`. The web servers (`web_server_0` through `web_server_3`) were healthy throughout — Apache running, port 80 listening, correct content served — so rebooting them would have had zero effect.

**Root cause:** The `named` service failed to come up (systemd `Active: failed`) on `dns_server` at lab initialization, leaving the entire lab without DNS resolution.

**Corrective fix:** Run `service named start` (or `systemctl start named`) on `dns_server`. Once started, the daemon correctly binds to 10.200.0.2:53, resolves `web0.local → 10.200.0.3` and `web1.local → 10.200.0.4`, and HTTP access immediately succeeds. To make the fix persistent, ensure the underlying cause of the startup failure (e.g., an ordering race at boot) is addressed and that the service is properly enabled.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states the BIND (`named`) daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) was in a failed/stopped state causing name resolution to fail and exonerates the web servers.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states the web servers were reachable by IP and Apache was running/listening, rejecting the 'web servers crashed' hypothesis.
Starts the BIND/named service on dns_server to restore DNS resolution, which matches the expected remediation.
